chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described, and how can He be described?
And He said in His Book: 'And they did not estimate Allah with the estimation that is due to Him,' so He would not be described with any estimation except that it would be less than that.

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cannot be described, and how can one describe a servant whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has veiled with seven (veils), and made obedience to him on earth like obedience to Him in the sky?

So He said: 'And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and from whatever he forbids you, keep back,' and 'Whoever obeys this one has obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Me,' and He delegated authority to him.
And we cannot be described, and how can one describe a group of people whom Allah has removed the filth from, and it is doubt?

And the believer cannot be described. And indeed, when a believer meets his brother and shakes his hand, Allah does not cease looking at them both, and sins fall from their faces just as leaves fall from the tree.

key_terms.حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ: With the estimation that is due to Him

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of shaking hands between believers in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrine of *la yuwsaf* (inexpressibility), extending the transcendence of Allah to the Prophet, the Imams, and the general believer, thereby elevating their spiritual status beyond human limitation. It uniquely links the theological concept of divine veiling (*hijab*) with the practical ethic of brotherhood, illustrating that physical gestures like handshaking serve as mechanisms for the shedding of sins, a theme resonating with the Quranic imagery of leaves falling from trees.
